16.25Context-Specific Parameters and Missing Information ​

In briefA framework may require an observation window, but cannot arbitrarily determine how many days each organization should observe, who has decision authority, or who should receive private material. When parameters are missing, identify which step cannot currently proceed while preserving supported conclusions that do not depend on them.

External procedures in each setting must determine who participates in consensus and its time limits, the observation windows, samples, and decision makers for restoring empirical question families, and safe channels, custodians, and remedial institutions for weak signals. They must also determine risk weights for gaps in AI outputs and criteria for comparisons with alternatives across disciplines, cultures, and jurisdictions. Registration must state the applicable organization, jurisdiction, object, risk level, evidence base, validity period, and review conditions. Numbers from one setting must not be copied into universal thresholds. If these fields are missing, the conclusion remains downgraded, suspended, or subject to competition. The framework must not fill them in itself.

A missing parameter blocks only judgments and uses that depend on it. Other conclusions with independent grounds are retained within their own scope. Keep unknowns preserved for protection, lack of the ability to observe, genuine inapplicability, and outstanding evidence needs separate. In actual use, also assess proportionality by comparing whether extra recording can change the judgment and reduce harm with the delays, exposure, and maintenance costs it creates.

16.25Note

Understanding this section

16.25 Context-specific parameters and handling missing values

A framework may require an observation window, but cannot arbitrarily determine how many days each organization should observe, who has decision authority, or who should receive private material. When parameters are missing, identify which step cannot currently proceed while preserving supported conclusions that do not depend on them.

Context-specific parameters connect general requirements to particular organizations and authorities. The source lists five groups that must be determined through external procedures for the particular context: consensus participants and time limits; the observation window, sample, and decision-makers needed to restore an empirical problem family; safe weak-signal channels, custodians, and remedy institutions; risk weights among missing AI items; and standards for comparing alternatives across disciplines, cultures, and jurisdictions. The framework can identify questions and evidentiary responsibilities, but cannot generate a valid threshold merely because its text needs a number.

These parameters require external determination because they involve actual participation eligibility, risks, resources, authority, and comparisons of values. Decision cycles, jurisdictions, and protective needs differ between organizations. Without participants and time limits, consensus completion is difficult to determine; without a restoration window and sample, an empirical problem family cannot arbitrarily be declared reliably eligible again; without safe channels and custodial responsibility, submitting weak signals may increase exposure; without risk weights and comparison standards, tradeoffs among gaps or alternatives lack public grounds. External procedures must themselves have concrete validity: asking an arbitrary person for a number is not adequate external determination.

Registration must specify seven applicability conditions: organization, jurisdiction, object, risk level, evidentiary basis, validity period, and review conditions. Organization and jurisdiction limit the institutional settings of use; object prevents mixing different populations or tasks; risk level explains the required rigor; evidentiary basis states the grounds for the parameter; and validity period and review conditions prevent old values from being retained forever. Thirty days being valid in one place does not establish thirty days elsewhere. Significant contextual change within the same organization also requires review, rather than reliance on the unchanged name.

When fields are missing, conclusions remain downgraded, suspended, or competing; the framework or AI must not fill them automatically. Pending items may be listed explicitly, with who should obtain them and which outputs they affect, but casually assigned defaults must not be hidden as already authorized context-specific parameters. Assumed values for teaching or sensitivity analysis are permissible if consistently labeled assumptions without acquiring eligibility for real-world clearance. A calculation running does not establish the parameters’ governance validity.

The scope of blocking from missing information follows dependencies. An undetermined restoration window blocks a restoration judgment that depends on it, but does not automatically invalidate a date independently supported by an original record. Conversely, when the gap concerns a shared source’s identity, lawful use conditions for the entire task, or a parameter shared by all outputs, blocking may be extensive. The principle of localization must not be used to evade shared gaps by splitting or renaming; nor should one local gap crudely erase all grounded content.

Four kinds of absence must remain separate: protective unknown means information is not obtained or disclosed for justified protection such as safety or privacy; lack of observational capacity means there is currently no corresponding measurement or acquisition route; genuine inapplicability means the item has no applicable object within the task boundary; and awaiting supplementary evidence means relevant evidence still needs to be obtained. None automatically means nonoccurrence or a value of zero. Protective unknowns especially must not justify forced disclosure. Genuine inapplicability needs a scope explanation; unwillingness to check cannot be packaged as inapplicability.

Records must also be proportionate. Whether a new field may change a judgment or reduce harm must be compared with waiting, exposure, and maintenance costs. A record that merely repeats an existing identity without adding verification value, yet requires another disclosure of sensitive experiences, may be inappropriate. Proportionality is not an excuse to delete necessary appeal, authorization, or risk records either. Consider reusing already authorized and applicable material, limiting collection, narrowing use, or retaining unknown status, rather than choosing only between unlimited collection and no records.

The strongest objection is that external determination of all parameters would prevent the framework from working. The response is to first complete material checks, candidate explanations, and comparison designs that do not depend on those parameters, while specifying which conclusions carrying greater responsibility cannot yet hold. This locates actual work better than pretending every parameter is available. Another objection says different contexts may set different values arbitrarily. That also fails: external procedures still must register evidence, applicability scope, and review conditions. Contextualization is not arbitrariness, nor does it turn normative gaps into author preferences.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Identify which of the five parameter groups this judgment actually depends on, and locate the specific external determination procedure.

  2. 2

    Register organization, jurisdiction, object, risk level, evidentiary basis, validity period, and review conditions.

  3. 3

    When parameters or applicability fields are missing, retain downgraded, suspended, or competing status; do not pass off defaults as valid decisions.

  4. 4

    Propagate restrictions along dependencies. Independently grounded conclusions retain their original scope; shared gaps must not be evaded by splitting tasks.

  5. 5

    Record protective unknown, lack of observational capacity, inapplicability, and pending evidence separately, and compare added records’ judgment benefits with waiting, exposure, and maintenance costs.

Distinctions to keep clear

Context-specific parameter

A value or rule determined through an applicable procedure, with scope, evidence, and a validity period.

≠

Framework default

May serve as an explicit teaching assumption, but does not automatically acquire real-world validity.

A local dependency is missing

Blocks judgments and uses specifically depending on that item.

≠

All content is invalid

Only failure of a shared or global premise extends to all dependent outputs.

Protective unknown

Justified protection restricts acquisition or disclosure.

≠

Awaiting supplementary evidence

Evidence still needs supplementation; authority and safety still apply, and disclosure cannot be forced.

Genuinely not applicable

The object and task scope make the item inapplicable; an explanation is required.

≠

Lack of observational capacity

The item may apply, but acquisition or measurement capacity is currently absent.

Proportionate records

The judgment and protection benefits of added material are sufficient relative to its costs.

≠

More is always better, or less is always better

The number of records does not itself establish governance quality.

Teaching construction: a missing window does not erase a date factTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThe date, module, and three days are hypothetical; three days is not a recommended threshold.

An imagined original record reliably establishes that a module was suspended on Monday, but the observation window and decision-maker required for restoration have not been determined through an applicable procedure. The fact “suspended on Monday” can be retained. Three elapsed days do not permit independently declaring three days sufficient and announcing restoration. The gap blocks restoration eligibility; it does not erase the independent date record.

BoundaryIf the date source’s identity is itself unverified, that fact needs separate downgrading.

Teaching construction: four kinds of blank are not the same zeroTeaching scenario

AssumptionsA, B, C, and D are recording situations, not personality or personnel categories; all are constructed.

In an imagined table, A omits sensitive details to protect the person; B lacks measurement tools; C is inapplicable because the relevant activity is absent; and D awaits supplementary documents from an authorized source. All four cells may look blank, but should be recorded separately as protective unknown, lack of observational capacity, not applicable, and awaiting supplementary evidence. They cannot all be scored as zero, whether they concern four people or four items.

BoundaryNecessary state records should also minimize exposure; protective unknowns need not be filled in.

Teaching construction: repeated registration increases exposureTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThe situation and proof are hypothetical; no real sensitive information was processed.

Suppose a check already has valid proof whose reuse is permitted, but a second form demands a complete repetition of a sensitive account that cannot change any decision. Examine whether a secure reference to the existing proof or reduced duplicate collection would suffice, while retaining necessary review entry points.

BoundaryReuse is permissible only when reuse itself is authorized and applicable; cost savings must not expand data access.

Actual contextualization guidance: NIST risk tolerance and resource allocationDocumented case

The About section of GOVERN 1.3 in the NIST AI RMF Playbook explains that governance resources are limited and that risk tolerance may range from negligible to severe losses. Suggested Actions calls for defining impact and likelihood assessments and qualitative or quantitative risk scales, recognizing that risk tolerance and risk levels change over the lifecycle. This illustrates risk-scale arrangements requiring organizational registration and review, rather than providing fixed numerical thresholds shared by every institution.

SourceNIST official AI RMF Playbook Govern page; accessed 2026-10-14First three paragraphs of GOVERN 1.3 About; all five Suggested Actions, especially the final itemReading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsSupports only that the guidance calls for managing risk scales according to organizational context. It does not establish implementation by any organization, nor is NIST’s illustrative risk-combination formula treated as this framework’s universal scoring rule or current law.

What it limitsContextual values require checking object risks and applicable procedures; they cannot be directly universalized.

What it limitsProtective unknowns have safety or privacy grounds; they must not justify forced disclosure or removal of the corresponding rights entry point.

What does not follow

  • A value from one context must not be copied into a universal threshold, nor may risk weights be automatically generated for real-world clearance.
  • The four kinds of absence mean neither zero nor factual negation; protective unknowns must not be forcibly converted into disclosure.
  • A local gap limits local dependencies, but missing shared global conditions affect every dependent output.
  • Inapplicability requires grounds in object scope; it must not become a label for evading checks.
  • This lesson determines no real organization’s deadlines, risk weights, authorized personnel, or remedy institutions.

Scope and open questions

The same official page is cited as in 16.23, but the additional focus is GOVERN 1.3’s contextual risk scales and review, rather than human-oversight responsibilities.

  • No actual organization, jurisdiction, object, risk level, or external determination procedure has been specified; this lesson cannot provide real-world parameters.

What work can continue when a restoration observation window is missing?

Independently sourced facts may be checked, candidates and gaps organized, and comparisons prepared. Eligibility for restoration that depends on the window cannot be declared satisfied.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

Why is inapplicability different from lack of observational capacity?

The former means the object scope does not require the item; the latter means it may apply but cannot currently be obtained. Their subsequent evidentiary responsibilities differ.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

Do more records mean greater safety?

Not necessarily. Assess whether they can change judgments and reduce harm, alongside waiting, exposure, and maintenance costs; necessary safeguards must not be casually deleted.
